opening: The cabinet has chosen to fix ageing bridges and locks over building new ones, leaving Friesland, Brabant and Amsterdam without projects they were promised. Ahold Delhaize has finally gone to the police over its cyberattack, regional buses strike again on Thursday, and doctors have quit an asylum shelter where people with severe mental illness are being housed.

stories.threadTitle: Roads, rail and the repair bill
stories.threadSummary: How the cabinet pays to keep ageing bridges, locks and tunnels safe, and which new projects have to wait.
stories.title: The cabinet puts repairs first and shelves 29 road, rail and water projects
stories.body: Infrastructure Minister Vincent Karremans and State Secretary Bertram will spend about €18 billion renovating and replacing ageing bridges, locks, viaducts and tunnels, most of them built between the 1950s and the 1970s. To pay for it, 29 planned projects lose their funding for now, among them a wider lock at Kornwerderzand in the Afsluitdijk, a faster ferry to Ameland, a new rail bridge at Leeuwarden, the N65 between Den Bosch and Tilburg and the northern part of Amsterdam's Zuidasdok. Provinces and cities spent the weekend voicing their frustration.
stories.whatChanged: The cabinet has chosen maintenance over expansion: money set aside for 29 new projects now goes to fixing structures that are wearing out.
stories.whyMatters: Many of the 175 structures in the plan are near the end of their working life, so delay risks closures; but the projects pushed back were meant to ease traffic, shipping and access to the islands, and some will cost more when they restart.
stories.uncertainty: Reports differ on the total (€16 billion or €18 billion), only some of the 29 postponed projects have been named, and parliament has not yet debated the plan.
stories.watchNext: The Tweede Kamer debate after the autumn recess, Amsterdam's talks with the minister on Zuidasdok, and whether provinces offer their own money to rescue projects.
keyFacts: 175 roads, locks, bridges, viaducts and tunnels are in the plan; most date from the 1950s to the 1970s
29 planned projects lose their funding for now; 16 new projects are still funded this term
Friesland misses about €635 million in investment, by the Leeuwarder Courant's count
€81 million had been reserved for the N65 between Den Bosch and Tilburg, now delayed for the sixth time in under three years, Brabant says
Still funded: the Nedersaksenlijn rail link between Groningen and Twente, and five A76 viaducts in South Limburg

report.heading: What the cabinet decided
paragraphs: On Friday 16 October, Minister Vincent Karremans and State Secretary Bertram of Infrastructure and Water Management presented a plan to spend about €18 billion maintaining and renewing the country's ageing infrastructure. It covers 175 roads, locks, bridges, viaducts and tunnels, most of them built in the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s, as well as money for the rail network. RTL Nieuws, quoted by NL Times, put the maintenance and renewal part at €16 billion. Rijkswaterstaat's roadmap lists 169 structures that need work; this term the cabinet aims to renovate 60 of them and maintain 59 more, with another 50 projects already being prepared or built.

Much of the money comes from projects that were planned but not yet started. Twenty-nine of them move to the bottom of the priority list. The cabinet says they are "not off the radar", but they have no funding for now. Only 16 new projects are funded this term, including the Nedersaksenlijn rail line between Groningen and Twente and infrastructure for large housing sites in places such as Deventer, Alkmaar and Weert.

report.heading: What has to wait
paragraphs: Friesland is hit hardest. The widening of the Kornwerderzand lock in the Afsluitdijk, which the national government itself pushed for in 2008, will not go ahead, and the faster ferry route to Ameland is not funded. The replacement of the old railway bridge over the Van Harinxmakanaal at Leeuwarden, for which €80 million of national money and €25 million from the region had been set aside, is off the list. The Leeuwarder Courant calculated that the province misses about €635 million in investment.

In Brabant, the upgrade of the N65 between Den Bosch and Tilburg is postponed despite €81 million reserved for it. In Amsterdam, the northern section of Zuidasdok, the combined expansion of Amsterdam Zuid station and widening of the A10, has no money for now, although work already under way continues. NL Times also lists the Utrecht ring road among the postponed projects.

report.heading: The reaction
paragraphs: Ameland's acting mayor, Tytsy Willemsma, called the decision "extremely disappointing", saying it had been clear for more than ten years that the island's ferry connection is not sustainable. Superyacht builder Sijbrand de Vries, who has waited years for a wider lock at Kornwerderzand, called it a hard blow. Brabant's provincial executive Stijn Smeulders told ANP it was "the sixth time in barely three years" that the N65 had been delayed. In Leeuwarden, alderman Evert Stellingwerf called the bridge decision disappointing and is pushing for extra money.

Zeeland, South Holland and the Rotterdam–The Hague metropolitan region said in a joint statement that they had hoped for a longer-term vision and more investment in motorway widening and public transport. Amsterdam alderman Moeskops warned that delaying Zuidasdok could add hundreds of millions of euros to its cost and leave the city with "a construction site and traffic gridlock for longer"; he expects to meet the minister soon.

report.heading: What comes next
paragraphs: The Tweede Kamer will debate the plans after the autumn recess. The problem the cabinet is trying to get ahead of is also local: an Omroep Gelderland survey published on Monday found that at least ten Gelderland municipalities do not know whether they own concrete bridges from the 1950s and 1960s with the kind of prestressing steel that can become brittle, the type of failure behind the collapse of the Carolabrücke in Dresden in 2024.

stories.threadSummary: The attack that took Albert Heijn, Etos and Gall & Gall systems offline, and how the company and investigators respond.
stories.title: Ahold Delhaize goes to the police a week after its cyberattack; Albert Heijn deliveries due back Friday
stories.body: Ahold Delhaize, the parent company of Albert Heijn, Etos and Gall & Gall, filed a police report on Monday about what it calls "a malicious action by third parties", more than a week after it detected suspicious activity and took systems offline. Police and prosecutors had publicly urged it to do so. The Albert Heijn website and app work again, and home delivery, halted since the attack, is due to restart on Friday. The company says it has found no sign so far that sensitive customer, staff or partner data was stolen.
stories.whatChanged: The company has now gone to the police, opening the way to a criminal investigation, and has set Friday for home deliveries to restart.
stories.whyMatters: Albert Heijn is the country's biggest supermarket chain, and the attack is an early test of the new cybersecurity rules that required the company to report it to the National Cyber Security Centre within 24 hours.
stories.uncertainty: Ahold Delhaize has not said whether this was ransomware, how the attackers got in or which brands abroad were affected, and its finding that no sensitive data was taken is provisional.
stories.watchNext: Whether deliveries restart on Friday as planned, what the police investigation finds, and whether customers have moved to rivals in the meantime.
keyFacts: Suspicious activity was detected early in the week of 12 October and some systems were taken offline
The National Cyber Security Centre was told within 24 hours, as the law requires
The police report was filed on 19 October, after police and prosecutors publicly called for one
The Albert Heijn app and website are back; Etos and Gall & Gall sites returned a week after the incident
Home delivery is expected to restart on Friday 23 October

report.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Ahold Delhaize detected suspicious activity early last week, brought in outside cyber experts and took some systems offline. The website and app of Albert Heijn became unreachable, as did those of drugstore chain Etos and liquor chain Gall & Gall, and brands elsewhere in Europe and in the United States were also affected, NOS reports. Chief executive Frans Muller said taking the systems offline was the right decision.

The app and website are working again, but home delivery has stayed suspended. Its restart was postponed again on Sunday and is now expected on Friday. NL Times reports that the Etos and Gall & Gall websites came back online a week after the incident.

report.heading: The report to the police
paragraphs: The company notified the National Cyber Security Centre within 24 hours of discovering the attack, a legal duty under the new cybersecurity law. It waited more than a week, however, before filing a report with the police. Last week the police and the Public Prosecution Service publicly urged it to come forward, saying a report was needed to investigate and prosecute successfully. Ahold Delhaize did not explain why it filed on Monday.
In its statement the company describes the incident as "a malicious action by third parties". It has not said whether a ransom was demanded, and its own investigation is continuing.

report.heading: What is still unclear
paragraphs: Ahold Delhaize says it has found no indication so far that sensitive data of customers, employees or partners was stolen. It has not named the foreign brands that were hit, given figures on lost sales, or said how the attackers got in.

stories.threadTitle: Asylum reception and the new asylum laws
stories.threadSummary: How the Netherlands houses and treats asylum seekers, and how the new asylum laws change the system.
stories.title: Doctors quit as asylum seekers with severe mental illness are sent to the strictest shelter
stories.body: The asylum agency COA is increasingly housing people with schizophrenia, psychosis, severe trauma and suicidal thoughts at its "enforcement and supervision location" in Hoogeveen, a strict regime meant for residents who cause trouble in other shelters, NRC reported on Monday. Three doctors have quit in the past year, saying their objections were ignored for years. COA and the asylum seekers' health service GZA confirmed that residents with serious mental illness live there and blamed long waiting lists and staff shortages in psychiatric care.
stories.whatChanged: COA has confirmed that psychiatric illness no longer automatically rules out placement in the strict shelter, and that residents there often do not get treatment in time.
stories.whyMatters: The Hoogeveen site has no psychiatrists or psychiatric nurses, and one of the doctors who left says he fears "a major incident"; the account adds to pressure on an asylum system the cabinet is tightening by law.
stories.uncertainty: NRC's account rests on three doctors who left and on COA's confirmation; COA has not published how many residents have a psychiatric illness, and the asylum minister has not yet responded.
stories.watchNext: A response from Asylum Minister Bart van den Brink, questions in the Tweede Kamer after the recess, and whether COA changes its placement rules.
keyFacts: The Hoogeveen location opened in 2020 for residents who cause problems in other asylum shelters
Residents must report daily, cannot leave freely and receive their allowance in goods, not cash
Three doctors have quit in the past year
The site has no psychiatrists or psychiatric nurses
COA says residents there "regularly" do not receive treatment in time or at all

report.heading: What NRC found
paragraphs: When the location in Hoogeveen opened in 2020, residents with psychiatric problems were not supposed to be placed there. That is no longer an automatic bar, although it can still be an obstacle. According to NRC, the site now houses people with schizophrenia, psychosis, severe trauma and suicidal tendencies, often despite objections from doctors.

Three doctors have resigned in the past year. They say they raised concerns with COA for four years and were dismissed. Doctor Marike Ooms left last summer after burning out following a week in which she treated three suicidal residents; she said the site is designed to confront residents with their behaviour, not to provide psychiatric care. Clara Verbeek, also a general practitioner, said she "couldn't take it anymore", and that some residents developed mental health problems while in the Dutch asylum system. A third doctor, who left last month after treating several residents in one week who needed a psychiatric hospital bed that could not be found, said: "Things cannot go on like this."

report.heading: The regime
paragraphs: The location is not a detention centre, but its rules are the strictest in Dutch asylum reception. Residents must check in every day, follow a mandatory daily schedule and cannot leave the premises freely. Their allowance is paid in goods. There are two disciplinary rooms for residents who are violent towards others or towards staff. Residents can leave by signing a COA form, but they then lose their right to accommodation.

report.heading: COA's answer
paragraphs: COA and the health service for asylum seekers, GZA, confirmed that the site houses residents with serious mental health problems, often with "psychiatric comorbidity". Both point to long waiting lists and staff shortages in specialised psychiatric care, and COA said residents there "regularly" do not get treatment in time, or at all.

report.heading: The wider system
paragraphs: The report comes as the cabinet tightens the asylum system by law. Last week the Eerste Kamer passed a new asylum law that, among other things, ends the penalty payments the immigration service IND owed when it missed decision deadlines; Asylum Minister Bart van den Brink said in September that the IND had paid out close to €100 million in such penalties. The minister has not yet responded to NRC's findings about Hoogeveen.

stories.threadSummary: The dispute over a new collective agreement for regional bus and train workers, and the weekly strikes it has brought.
stories.title: Regional buses and trains strike again on Thursday as pay talks stay stuck
stories.body: More than 13,500 regional public transport workers will stop work again on Thursday 22 October, union FNV says, the second strike day in just over a week in a dispute over a new collective agreement. Far fewer regional buses and trains will run. City transport in Amsterdam and Rotterdam, including Rotterdam's metro and trams, is expected to run as normal. FNV and CNV have said they want to strike one day a week until Christmas.
stories.whatChanged: A second strike day is confirmed after talks failed to move, turning a one-off stoppage into a weekly pattern.
stories.whyMatters: Outside the big cities, regional buses are often the only public transport; on the last strike day FNV says about 90 percent of buses did not run.
stories.uncertainty: How many services will be cancelled in each region is not yet known, and the unions and employers' organisation VWOV give different pictures of how many staff take part.
stories.watchNext: Operators' timetables for Thursday, any new offer from employers, and whether the unions name the next strike day.
keyFacts: More than 13,500 regional transport workers are involved, FNV says
The previous strike day was Wednesday 14 October
The unions want a pay rise, rosters announced further ahead and better conditions for older staff
Urban transport in Amsterdam and Rotterdam is expected to run
FNV and CNV plan one strike day a week until Christmas

report.heading: The strike
paragraphs: Regional transport workers will stop work again on Thursday, FNV announced on Monday, after a strike the previous week. Far fewer regional buses and trains will run that day. Public transport in the big cities, including Amsterdam and Rotterdam, should run as usual; AD reports that Rotterdam's metro and trams will run normally, while in Utrecht buses and trams may be affected, according to DUIC.

"The employers are still not listening well enough," Marijn van der Gaag, who leads FNV's regional transport section, told NOS. In a press release he said the employers "will not abandon deteriorations, so striking is the only option left".

report.heading: What the unions want
paragraphs: The talks on a new collective agreement are deadlocked. FNV's demands include a pay rise, work schedules announced further in advance, and better conditions for older employees, including more freedom to choose which days they work.

report.heading: Last week's strike
paragraphs: On Wednesday 14 October, FNV says about 90 percent of buses nationwide did not run. Employers' organisation VWOV said half of employees were willing to strike. In Almere some buses ran but trips were cancelled, according to 1Almere, and travellers in Leeuwarden were warned to expect cancellations, Omroep Leeuwarden reported.

stories.threadSummary: What parents pay for childcare, how the allowance keeps up, and the planned overhaul of the system.
stories.title: Childcare prices rise faster than the allowance, and low earners pay the most
stories.body: Childcare providers will charge an average of €11.82 an hour next year, 22 cents above the €11.60 maximum on which the government bases its childcare allowance, according to a survey of 400 providers by parents' group BOinK, reported by NU.nl. Parents pay the difference. For low-income families, whose allowance covers 96 percent of the maximum rate, the cost of an hour of childcare would rise from about 45 cents to about 68 cents.
stories.whatChanged: New survey figures show the gap between what providers charge and what the allowance covers widening again for 2027.
stories.whyMatters: BOinK warns that low-income families, who already use childcare much less than others, will feel the increase most.
stories.uncertainty: The figures are averages from a survey of providers and individual rates vary; the ministry argues that the gap between the maximum and average prices has narrowed since 2023.
stories.watchNext: The Tweede Kamer's budget debates after the recess, and the planned 2029 overhaul of the allowance.
keyFacts: Maximum hourly rate for the allowance: €11.23 this year, €11.60 in 2027
Average provider rate in 2027: €11.82, according to BOinK's survey of 400 organisations
Low-income parents' own cost: about 45 cents an hour now, about 68 cents in 2027
From 2029, middle and high incomes are due to get 95.6 percent of the maximum reimbursed; low incomes drop slightly from 96 percent to 95.6

report.heading: The numbers
paragraphs: This year the government's maximum hourly rate for daycare is €11.23, and low-income families are reimbursed 96 percent of it, leaving them to pay 45 cents an hour if their provider charges no more than the maximum. Next year the maximum rises to €11.60. But providers will charge €11.82 on average, BOinK found, and parents must pay everything above the maximum themselves. For low-income households that means about 68 cents an hour. Higher-income families pay more as well, but can absorb it more easily.
"This is bad news, as childcare usage among low-income groups is already significantly lower," BOinK chair Gjalt Jellesma said.

report.heading: The ministry's view
paragraphs: A spokesperson for the Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment said it is "not the intention that all costs should be shifted entirely onto the taxpayer". The ministry says the allowance is deliberately not linked to price rises, because that could encourage providers to raise prices, and argues that childcare is becoming more affordable because the gap between the maximum and average rates has narrowed since 2023.

report.heading: What changes in 2029
paragraphs: Under the planned new system, middle- and high-income families will be reimbursed 95.6 percent of the benchmark rate. Low-income families will move slightly down, from 96 percent to 95.6 percent.

stories.title: Groningen and North Drenthe ask JA21 to drop a bill that would keep the gas field on standby
stories.whatChanged: The governments of the earthquake region have formally objected to a JA21 plan to reverse the field's permanent closure.
stories.body: JA21 MP Daniël van den Berg's bill would make the Groningen field an emergency gas reserve and overturn the 2024 decision to close it for good: wells would stay available, small "readiness" extraction would keep the field usable, and emergency extraction would be possible in a gas crisis. Provincial executive Susan Top, speaking for the region's governments, said it "runs counter to the fresh start promised to residents of Groningen and Noord-Drenthe" and would unsettle decisions on reinforcing homes, without clarity on damage and liability. The region says it understands the need for secure supply but does not expect extra Groningen gas to move international prices.

stories.title: Schiphol's passport gates went down for most of Sunday, and the cause will stay secret
stories.whatChanged: The Marechaussee is investigating why all 78 automatic passport gates failed on Sunday, but says it will not publish the findings.
stories.body: All 78 e-gates at Schiphol went down at about 6am on Sunday, in the middle of the autumn school holiday, and passengers to and from countries outside the Schengen area had to be checked by hand until the gates came back at about 3pm. Hundreds of people missed flights and waits averaged an hour. The Royal Marechaussee blames an IT fault, says there is "no indication whatsoever" of a cyberattack, and will not release its investigation "for operational reasons". Experts told De Telegraaf few travellers are likely to get compensation.

stories.title: Police seek the man seen cycling with Hajar, 29, whose body was found in a suitcase in Amsterdam
stories.whatChanged: Police confirmed that Hajar was found in a suitcase in the water at the Amsteldijk; no one has been arrested.
stories.body: Hajar was last seen on 4 October near the RAI, cycling with an unidentified man towards Buitenveldert; her family reported her missing the next day. Her body was found on Friday morning in a suitcase in the water at the Amsteldijk in Amsterdam-Zuid. Police say she died as the result of a crime but do not know where, are looking for the man she was seen with, according to NH Nieuws, and have asked residents whether they saw anyone with a suitcase in recent weeks. Her family has asked to grieve in private.

stories.title: Grolsch visitors who fell ill had swallowed caustic soda from a tasting tap
stories.whatChanged: Investigators confirmed that cleaning fluid containing sodium hydroxide reached a tap where visitors taste brewing water.
stories.body: Eleven people fell ill during a brewery tour in Enschede on Saturday. Grolsch says diluted cleaning fluid, used in the three-weekly cleaning of the pipe that feeds the tasting tap, reached the tap because the connection lacked a technical safety lock. Everyone has left hospital, though some still have a sore throat or have lost their sense of taste. Police have ended their inquiry; the Labour Inspectorate is still investigating. Grolsch says no caustic soda got into its beer and is considering compensation.

stories.title: A judge bars ING from dropping Gazprom as a client
stories.whatChanged: ING must keep Gazprom's account open until the Russian company finds another European bank, a judge ruled.
stories.body: ING ended the relationship at the end of 2023, citing sanctions, money-laundering and reputational risks after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Gazprom is not on the EU sanctions list, and argued it had no other European account, without which it cannot pay taxes or the wages of its European staff. The judge found no concrete evidence of money-laundering risk. ING is also still struggling to sell its Russian subsidiary.

stories.title: Another night of unrest in Amsterdam's Floradorp over a banned bonfire
stories.whatChanged: Stones and bottles were thrown at police on Monday night after the mayor rejected a smaller alternative to the neighbourhood's traditional bonfire.
stories.body: Residents gathered on Sneeuwbalstraat in the late afternoon, setting off fireworks and lighting small fires in the road and in underground bins; later, stones and glass bottles were thrown at police and riot police were called in. A 39-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of throwing fireworks at officers, and a 14-year-old boy for public violence. The unrest followed a letter from Mayor Femke Halsema turning down residents' proposal for a small fire in an open container, on the fire service's advice; the bonfire was banned last year. Het Parool reports that a death in the neighbourhood also plays a part.

stories.title: Coos Huijsen, the first openly gay member of parliament, has died at 87
stories.whatChanged: Huijsen, who came out when he took his seat in the Tweede Kamer in 1976, died at home after a short illness.
stories.body: Huijsen entered the Tweede Kamer for the CHU in 1972, left the party months later over its refusal to back the Den Uyl cabinet, and returned as an independent in 1976, when he came out; he and his family say he was the first openly gay member of any parliament. He later taught history and led the Gerrit van der Veen College in Amsterdam, earned a doctorate on the House of Orange, and co-founded Het Blauwe Fonds for gay emancipation. His husband, Lank Bos, was with him.

stories.threadSummary: Why so many homes, firms and public services wait for a grid connection, and who gets one first.
stories.title: Data centres take up nearly a third of the queue for the power grid
stories.body: Grid operators told NOS's Nieuwsuur that data centres account for almost a third of the capacity requested on the waiting list for new or bigger grid connections. The whole list adds up to about 15 gigawatts, roughly the combined connection capacity of all Dutch households. Netbeheer Nederland, the grid operators' association, wants the government to decide how many data centres the country should host, and where.
stories.whatChanged: Grid operators have put a figure on the data-centre share of the grid queue and asked the government to choose between users.
stories.whyMatters: Expanding the grid is estimated to cost more than €200 billion and take years, so capacity given to data centres is capacity that factories, housing and public services wait longer for.
stories.hook: A full grid turns every new data centre into a choice about who else has to wait.
stories.uncertainty: The figures do not fully reconcile: the 15 GW total is well above the 9,986 MW that businesses requested through regional operators, and the scope of each number is not explained.
stories.watchNext: State Secretary Jo-Annes de Bat's measures to free up capacity faster, and whether the cabinet sets limits on where data centres may go.
keyFacts: About 15 GW of capacity is on the waiting list in total
15,498 businesses were waiting for large connections through regional operators in the first half of 2026, asking for 9,986 MW
There are almost 200 large and about 300 smaller data centres, with about 200 more expected
The largest uses about as much electricity as 1 percent of Dutch households
Expanding the grid is estimated to cost more than €200 billion

report.heading: The queue
paragraphs: Companies that want a new or heavier grid connection join a waiting list. According to the grid operators, data centres account for almost one third of the capacity on it. In total, about 15 gigawatts is requested, roughly the combined connection capacity of every Dutch household. In the first half of 2026, 15,498 businesses were waiting for large connections through regional grid operators, together requesting 9,986 megawatts, up from 9,305 MW at the end of 2025.
The Netherlands has almost 200 large and around 300 smaller data centres, and about 200 more are expected. The largest uses about as much electricity as roughly 1 percent of Dutch households.

report.heading: Why operators want a choice
paragraphs: Grid operators have to decide years in advance where to lay cables and build substations, and say the queue makes that planning hard when they cannot tell which projects will go ahead. "We live in a time of scarcity: not everything can be everywhere," said Joris de Groot of Alliander, speaking for Netbeheer Nederland, comparing the problem to the nitrogen debate. "The government must therefore make choices about where we still want data centers."
The pressure shows up in unexpected places. In Almere, a full grid is delaying the switch to new rubbish trucks; the city expects to rent vehicles for the next four years, 1Almere reported on Monday.

report.heading: What the government is doing
paragraphs: State Secretary for Climate and Green Growth Jo-Annes de Bat recently announced measures to free up grid capacity faster, after the Tweede Kamer pushed for a nationwide plan. Netbeheer Nederland says that is not enough without firmer decisions on how many data centres the country should accommodate and where they may operate.

stories.threadSummary: Who controls the data and digital services the Netherlands depends on, and how far foreign governments can reach into them.
stories.title: A server seized in Amsterdam at Washington's request tests Dutch digital sovereignty
stories.body: Police seized a server at Amsterdam Science Park belonging to Autistici/Inventati, an Italian email and hosting provider for activists that the United States has designated a terrorist organisation, at the request of the US authorities. The Dutch Cloud Community, the sector's trade association, has sent the police a letter demanding to know the legal basis, warning that without a clear Dutch review "the Netherlands loses trust" as a place to store data. Prosecutors say the seizure followed the Dutch–US mutual legal assistance treaty and that the data has not yet been shared.
stories.whatChanged: A US request has led Dutch police to seize a European provider's server, and the cloud sector is openly questioning whether Dutch law checked it.
stories.whyMatters: The Dutch data-centre and cloud industry sells itself on the protection of Dutch and European law; the case lands days after the government again blocked the sale of DigiD supplier Solvinity to a US company over similar fears.
stories.hook: If a foreign request can reach a server in Amsterdam without a clear Dutch check, data stored here is only as safe as that check.
stories.uncertainty: The prosecution has not published its assessment, the data-centre operator has not been named, and it is not known what the US is seeking from the data.
stories.watchNext: The police and prosecution's answer to the Dutch Cloud Community, whether the data is handed over, and questions in parliament after the recess.
keyFacts: The server was seized in Amsterdam-Oost, at Amsterdam Science Park
Autistici/Inventati offered free email and hosting to about 20,000 activists and organisations for some 25 years, and dissolved itself after US sanctions in late August
Prosecutors say the seizure was made under the Dutch–US mutual legal assistance treaty and found no ground for refusal
On 13 October the government blocked US firm Kyndryl's purchase of DigiD supplier Solvinity for the second time

report.heading: The seizure
paragraphs: The server belongs to Autistici/Inventati (A/I), an Italian provider that describes itself as anti-capitalist and anti-fascist. For about 25 years it offered free email and web hosting, mainly to activists and civil-rights groups, reaching around 20,000 organisations and individuals worldwide. The United States designated it a terrorist organisation, alleging it serves "extreme left-wing organisations", including "Antifa cells". After US sanctions in late August, A/I lost its domain, its PayPal account and its bank account, and dissolved itself more than a week later. Its Italian bank, Banca Etica, closed the account for fear of US secondary sanctions while condemning the US action.

Dutch police then seized one of its servers at Amsterdam Science Park at the request of the US authorities. In a statement to ANP, the Public Prosecution Service said the seizure was carried out under the mutual legal assistance treaty between the Netherlands and the United States, that there was no ground for refusal, and that the data has not been shared with the US yet.

report.heading: The sector's objection
paragraphs: The Dutch Cloud Community sent the police a letter asking for the legal basis of the seizure and how it was carried out. It says the case appears to give the US a free pass to request data without clear, independent Dutch legal review, and warns that international cooperation against crime must not be used to suppress political expression. "Without a clear Dutch review, the Netherlands loses trust," the association said.

report.heading: A pattern of concern
paragraphs: The case follows a government decision on 13 October to block, for the second time, the sale of Solvinity, which runs infrastructure for part of the DigiD login system, to the American company Kyndryl. State Secretary for Digital Economy Willemijn Aerdts concluded the takeover could threaten the public interest; members of parliament fear US rules could allow Washington to shut DigiD down.

sources.title: Nederlandse cloudsector eist opheldering over inbeslagname server op verzoek VS

stories.threadSummary: Demand for new weight-loss medicines, who can get them, and the risks of buying them outside the pharmacy.
stories.title: An unapproved weight-loss drug spreads through TikTok, and doctors warn of the risks
stories.body: Hundreds of people in the Netherlands are estimated to be injecting retatrutide, an experimental weight-loss drug not approved in Europe, De Telegraaf reports. It found ten TikTok accounts selling jars of powder, and one seller said sales grew from a few jars a day in January to more than 100. The European Medicines Agency has received no application to approve the drug. The health inspectorate IGJ says people in the Netherlands have been hospitalised, and some have died, after using illegal medication.
stories.whatChanged: An experimental drug still in research is being sold openly online in the Netherlands, mixed at home by buyers.
stories.whyMatters: Demand for newer weight-loss drugs is running ahead of approval and access; buyers get powders of unknown content and purity and dose them themselves, where a simple miscalculation can mean an overdose.
stories.hook: Demand for the next weight-loss drug is running ahead of the evidence, and buyers are doing their own dosing.
stories.uncertainty: User numbers are estimates from De Telegraaf's reporting, and the IGJ's figures on hospital admissions and deaths concern illegal medication in general, not retatrutide specifically.
stories.watchNext: Whether the IGJ or customs act against the sellers, and whether TikTok removes the accounts.
keyFacts: Retatrutide is experimental and not approved for the European market
Hundreds of people in the Netherlands are estimated to use it, mostly bought via TikTok
De Telegraaf found ten TikTok accounts selling it as powder
One seller reports sales rising from a few jars a day in January to over 100 a day, sourced from China and sold as a "research peptide"

report.heading: What is being sold
paragraphs: Retatrutide is still being researched as an obesity treatment and is not approved in Europe; the EMA has not received an application. Users told De Telegraaf it is cheaper and more effective than the alternatives they can get. The paper found ten TikTok accounts selling jars of the powder. One seller who uses his own website said his sales grew from a few jars a day in January to more than 100 a day. He buys stock from China and markets it as a "research peptide".

report.heading: The risks
paragraphs: "No one knows exactly what is inside the containers they order," said Gijs van Acker, medical director of the Dutch Obesity Clinic. The powder may not have been made under sterile conditions, and buyers mix it themselves, so a small miscalculation can lead to an overdose. "Essentially, you are gambling with your life," he said.

The IGJ warns about illegal weight-loss products and says people in the Netherlands have been hospitalised, and some have died, after using illegal medication. It advises anyone seeking help with weight loss to see their GP and to get medication only from a licensed pharmacy.

sources.title: Illegal weight-loss drug retatrutide on the rise in the Netherlands

image.alt: An unlabelled jar of white powder next to a syringe and a phone screen showing a shopping bag, for an unapproved weight-loss drug sold through social media.

stories.threadSummary: The long struggle to cut nitrogen emissions to protect nature, and what it means for livestock farmers.
stories.title: Nitrogen: most livestock farmers say the new rules have cost them faith in the future
stories.body: Eighty-seven percent of livestock farmers say the cabinet's new nitrogen plans have reduced their confidence in the future of their farms, according to a survey of nearly 600 farmers by RTL and the trade magazine Boerderij. Six in ten dairy farmers think they cannot meet the stricter standard, and only 6 percent trust the current cabinet. Yet most are open to cleaner feed and new technology, and the Tweede Kamer is preparing an emergency law to cut emissions quickly.
stories.whatChanged: A large survey shows how far trust has fallen as the cabinet prepares faster, stricter nitrogen rules.
stories.whyMatters: Nitrogen limits decide whether farms can stay, whether nature areas recover and whether housing and roads get permits; without farmers' cooperation the targets are hard to reach.
stories.uncertainty: The survey reached nearly 600 farmers who chose to respond, and the details of the cabinet's plan and the emergency law are still being worked out.
stories.watchNext: The emergency nitrogen law in the Tweede Kamer, and how Agriculture Minister Jaimi van Essen responds to farmers' doubts.
keyFacts: 87 percent say the new nitrogen plans have reduced their confidence in their farm's future
Six in ten dairy farmers think they cannot meet the stricter standard; 4 percent expect to meet it without major changes
63 percent may invest in emission-cutting technology; nearly three-quarters are open to lower-protein feed
6 percent trust the current cabinet and 7 percent trust Agriculture Minister Jaimi van Essen

report.heading: What farmers say
paragraphs: RTL and Boerderij surveyed nearly 600 livestock farmers. Eighty-seven percent said the cabinet's new nitrogen plans had reduced their confidence in the future of their farms. Six in ten dairy farmers believe they cannot meet the stricter standard; only 4 percent expect to meet it without major changes, and one in five think it is possible only with extra investment. One farmer wrote that meeting the requirements would mean investing more than €2.1 million, roughly doubling the mortgage.

Trust in government is very low: 6 percent have confidence in the current cabinet and 7 percent in Agriculture Minister Jaimi van Essen. Two-thirds say farmer protests should stay public-friendly, but one in five consider intimidating politicians and officials acceptable.

report.heading: Room for change
paragraphs: The survey also shows willingness to act. Sixty-three percent are potentially willing to invest in technology that cuts emissions, and nearly three-quarters are open to lower-protein feed, which can limit ammonia emissions. Many say the problem is the pace and the constant changes: "Every four years there are different rules," one farmer, Maaike, told RTL.

report.heading: What comes next
paragraphs: The Tweede Kamer is preparing an emergency law to reduce nitrogen emissions quickly. Farmers say that pace may be impossible to meet.

sources.title: 87% of Dutch livestock farmers lose faith in future over nitrogen rules

watch.title: Regional transport · October 22
watch.text: The second strike day in the regional bus and train dispute; watch how many services run outside the big cities and whether employers make a new offer.

watch.title: Albert Heijn · October 23
watch.text: Home deliveries are due to restart after the cyberattack; a further delay would suggest the systems are not yet fully restored.

watch.title: Tweede Kamer · after the recess
watch.text: MPs debate the infrastructure plan; watch whether a majority tries to rescue projects such as the Afsluitdijk lock, the Ameland ferry or the N65.

groningen.summary: The region's governments object to a JA21 plan to keep the gas field on standby, while the Nedersaksenlijn rail link to Twente keeps its funding. In the city, a party wants an inquiry into two deaths in a squalid care building.

briefs.title: City party wants inquiry into deaths in a Vinkhuizen care building
briefs.text: Stadspartij 100% voor Groningen wants an independent investigation into care at a building on Smaragdstraat, where a 26-year-old and a 42-year-old resident died within five days of each other in August 2025, as DvhN reported earlier this year. The municipality says it was not responsible for overseeing the care, which it says fell to health insurer Menzis.

sources.title: Stadspartij wil onafhankelijk onderzoek naar gang van zaken rond overleden bewoners in zorgpand Vinkhuizen

briefs.title: University of Groningen gets €1 million to study health in climate lawsuits
briefs.text: Researchers from the University of Groningen and Columbia Law School received €1 million from the Wellcome Trust to study how health damage features in climate cases worldwide, and to expand a database of about 4,000 climate cases from more than 55 countries.

sources.title: RUG krijgt miljoen euro voor onderzoek naar gezondheid in rechtszaken over klimaat

briefs.title: The Nedersaksenlijn survives the infrastructure cuts
briefs.text: The planned rail line between Groningen and Twente is one of only 16 new projects the cabinet still funds this term, while 29 others were postponed.

sources.title: No funding for 29 projects in gov't infrastructure plans, €16 billion for maintenance

friesland.summary: Friesland is the biggest loser in the cabinet's infrastructure choices: no wider Afsluitdijk lock, no faster Ameland ferry and no new rail bridge at Leeuwarden. The province also lost its longest-serving councillor.

briefs.title: Leeuwarden loses €105 million for a new rail bridge over the Van Harinxmakanaal
briefs.text: Minister Karremans has withdrawn the €80 million of national money that, with €25 million from the region, was to replace the old rail bridge with an aqueduct. A skipper's wheelhouse was torn off when the bridge closed on his barge in 2023. Alderman Evert Stellingwerf called the decision disappointing; inland shipping operators are angry.

sources.title: Leeuwarden krijgt geen geld voor vervanging oude spoorbrug over Van Harinxmakanaal

briefs.title: Rinze Visser, the country's longest-serving councillor, dies at 87
briefs.text: Visser, known as Fryslân's oldest communist, was first elected to the Lemsterland council in 1970 and was re-elected 14 times in a row, later in De Fryske Marren. He stepped down before the March 2026 elections; with no successor, communism no longer has an elected seat in Frisian politics.

sources.title: 'Fryslâns oudste communist' en langstzittende raadslid Rinze Visser (87) overleden

drenthe.summary: Doctors have quit the strict asylum location in Hoogeveen, North Drenthe joins Groningen against keeping the gas field on standby, and the Zuidlaardermarkt horse fair is under way.

briefs.title: A Qbuzz bus burns out at Hoogersmilde; everyone gets off in time
briefs.text: A diesel bus on the Assen–Steenwijk line caught fire on the N371 on Monday morning. The driver and all passengers got out unhurt; the cause is not yet known.

sources.title: Lijnbus uitgebrand in Hoogersmilde, passagiers komen met de schrik vrij

briefs.title: Extra night buses for the Zuidlaardermarkt
briefs.text: The Zuidlaardermarkt, the oldest and largest horse market in the Netherlands, runs on 19 and 20 October, with extra night buses between Zuidlaren and Assen, Vries, Eelde, Groningen, Hoogezand, Veendam and Gieten.

sources.title: Extra (nacht)bussen voor Zuidlaardermarkt

overijssel.summary: The illness on a Grolsch tour in Enschede was caused by caustic soda, Dutch and German police target heavy fireworks smuggled over the border, and the Nedersaksenlijn and a Deventer housing site keep their funding.

briefs.title: Dutch and German police step up the hunt for heavy fireworks in the border region
briefs.text: Explosives and heavy fireworks used in attacks in cities such as Amsterdam and Rotterdam come into the country via Germany and Belgium, AD reports. Police on both sides of the border are starting a new approach with more investigations, checks and seizures.

sources.title: Nederlandse en Duitse politie jagen in grensregio op zwaar vuurwerk: 'Explosieven uit handen georganiseerde misdaad'

briefs.title: Twente rail link and a Deventer housing site keep their money
briefs.text: The Nedersaksenlijn between Groningen and Twente and infrastructure for a large housing site in Deventer are among the 16 new projects the cabinet still funds this term.

sources.title: No funding for 29 projects in gov't infrastructure plans, €16 billion for maintenance

flevoland.summary: The state will move businesses and farmers to make room for F-35 fighters at Lelystad Airport, and residents of Almere and Lelystad feel less safe in their neighbourhoods than elsewhere in the Amsterdam region.

briefs.title: Six companies and four farmers must move for F-35s at Lelystad Airport
briefs.text: Defence will expand Lelystad Airport by 240 hectares, 200 for military facilities and 40 for a longer runway, to station F-35 fighter jets there. State Secretary Derk Boswijk said he understands the project has significant consequences for those affected.

sources.title: Gov't forcing 6 companies, 4 farmers to move to expand Lelystad Airport for F-35 use

briefs.title: Almere and Lelystad residents feel less safe than the regional average
briefs.text: According to the Economic Outlook for the Amsterdam Metropolitan Area 2026, people in Almere and Lelystad feel unsafe in their own neighbourhood more often than the regional average, and have less trust in other people and in institutions.

sources.title: Inwoners Almere en Lelystad voelen zich vaker onveilig in eigen buurt

briefs.title: Charging-point firm Blue Marble left €1.4 million in debts
briefs.text: The Almere company, declared bankrupt with three sister firms at the end of September, has more than €1.4 million in known debts, according to the receiver's first report cited by De Stentor. Separately, Flevoland says it sees little room for more asylum places and that other regions should take their turn.

sources.title: 1Almere in 1 minuut, 19 oktober 2026

gelderland.summary: Trains between Arnhem and Utrecht stop for 12 days from today, at least ten municipalities cannot say whether their bridges are brittle, and wolves are changing how deer and boar behave on the Veluwe.

briefs.title: No trains between Arnhem and Driebergen-Zeist until Friday
briefs.text: ProRail is maintaining track and building a railway underpass near Wolfheze. Until 23 October no trains run between Driebergen-Zeist and Arnhem Centraal or Rhenen; from 24 to 31 October the gap is Arnhem–Ede-Wageningen. NS runs replacement buses and suggests travelling via 's-Hertogenbosch or Deventer.

sources.title: Trains between Arnhem and Utrecht to be suspended for 12 days starting October 20

briefs.title: At least ten municipalities don't know whether they have brittle bridges
briefs.text: An Omroep Gelderland survey found that municipalities including Doetinchem, Lochem, Druten, Wijchen, Winterswijk and Tiel do not know whether they own 1950s and 1960s concrete bridges with prestressing steel that can become brittle. Most will not investigate; Druten and Wijchen will. TU Delft professor Hans Ramler called it striking.

sources.title: Survey: At least 10 Gelderland municipalities don't know if they have vulnerable bridges

briefs.title: Wolves make the Veluwe's deer and boar more alert
briefs.text: With just under a hundred wolves now on the Veluwe, wild boar move in larger groups and roe deer graze more at night, the Gelderland wildlife management unit says. The wolf slows the growth of boar numbers but not enough to stop the need for culling.

sources.title: Wolf maakt zwijnen en herten op Veluwe alerter: 'Vroeger zat er weinig pit in'

utrecht.summary: Train works cut the Utrecht–Arnhem line from today, the city's audit office says its road-safety policy lacks direction, and schools face cuts in money for pupils at risk of falling behind.

briefs.title: Audit office: Utrecht must steer its road-safety policy more clearly
briefs.text: The Rekenkamer Utrecht concludes that the city needs to direct its road-safety approach more clearly and carry it out more consistently. The number of traffic casualties is falling, but residents are less satisfied with road safety.

sources.title: Utrecht moet aanpak verkeersveiligheid beter aansturen en uitvoeren

briefs.title: Amersfoort school could lose a third of its disadvantage funding
briefs.text: A national redistribution of money for pupils at risk of falling behind may cost Amersfoort's Vlinderslag school more than €100,000, nearly a third of what it now receives. The city of Utrecht expects to lose €7.2 million a year from 2027 for the same reason.

sources.title: Minder geld voor Vlinderslag in Amersfoort: 'Dit raakt kinderen die het echt nodig hebben'
Utrecht verliest miljoenen voor onderwijs en kampt met groeiend tekort voor schoolgebouwen

briefs.title: UMC Utrecht team wins €50,000 to give voiceless patients their own voice back
briefs.text: The ReVoice project, started by Boudewijn Faber, who lost his voice to laryngeal cancer, uses AI to turn speech through a voice prosthesis into a voice resembling the patient's own, built from a few seconds of old recordings. The prize money will fund a first prototype.

sources.title: UMC Utrecht werkt aan techniek waarmee patiënten na stemverlies hun eigen stem terugkrijgen

north-holland.summary: Police are looking for a man seen with Hajar before she disappeared, Floradorp had another night of unrest, and Amsterdam's festivals say rising taxes are pricing out international guests.

briefs.title: Amsterdam festivals say higher taxes are hurting culture
briefs.text: IDFA, De Balie and the Holland Festival say rising hotel and travel costs make it harder to bring in international guests. Amsterdam plans to raise its tourist tax from 12.5 percent of the room price to 16 percent, and eventually 20, after a national VAT rise on overnight stays.

sources.title: Higher taxes further damaging Amsterdam culture sector, ADE, IDFA & other festivals warn

briefs.title: Man, 81, dies after a home robbery in Schagen; suspect caught in Obdam
briefs.text: The man was seriously injured in a robbery at his home on Groenling and died shortly after reaching hospital. Police boxed in the fleeing car between Heerhugowaard and Obdam and arrested a 36-year-old man with no fixed address.

sources.title: Man (81) overleden na woningoverval in Schagen, verdachte opgepakt

briefs.title: Zuidasdok delay could cost hundreds of millions, alderman warns
briefs.text: Amsterdam alderman Moeskops says postponing the northern part of Zuidasdok leaves the city with a building site and traffic jams for longer and risks losing the investment already made. He expects to meet Minister Karremans soon.

sources.title: Amsterdam alderman warns of rising costs as Cabinet postpones major Zuidasdok project

south-holland.summary: A final report finds a Leiden lab technician fathered 16 children with his own sperm, a car went off the Dordrecht ferry ramp for the fourth time since 2020, and the Calandbrug in the port is shut by another fault.

briefs.title: Leiden lab technician fathered 16 children, not 11, final report finds
briefs.text: MC Kinderwens' final report says the technician at its predecessor clinic used his own sperm between 1979 and 1984 under other donors' names, and carried two genetic conditions. Donor children told Omroep West the report plays down the risks.

sources.title: Leidse laborant verwekte niet 11 maar 16 kinderen met eigen zaad

briefs.title: Man dies after car goes into the water at the Dordrecht ferry ramp
briefs.text: Three occupants were pulled from the car at the ferry to Werkendam on Sunday evening; a 63-year-old man died in hospital. A woman died at the same spot in December 2024, and cars also went into the water there in 2020 and 2022. The road runs straight onto the ramp with no barrier.

sources.title: Opnieuw fataal ongeluk bij veerpontoprit Dordrecht, man (63) overleden

briefs.title: Calandbrug closed again after another fault
briefs.text: The rail and road bridge at Rozenburg in the Rotterdam port, closed for several days last week, broke down again; it was still shut to traffic and shipping on Tuesday morning. ProRail says it is unclear when the problem will be fixed.

sources.title: Weer een storing bij de Calandbrug: onduidelijk wanneer de problemen zijn opgelost

zeeland.summary: A man died in a flat fire in Terneuzen, a Belgian appeals court jailed the man who left four-year-old Dean's body on Neeltje Jans, and a powder found near the Covra nuclear-waste site proved harmless.

briefs.title: Man, 50, dies in a Terneuzen flat fire
briefs.text: The fire broke out on Saturday evening in a second-floor flat on Diepenbrockstraat and was under control within half an hour. All residents were evacuated and several homes are temporarily uninhabitable; the cause has not been made public.

sources.title: Dode bij woningbrand Terneuzen, meerdere appartementen onbewoonbaar

briefs.title: Thirty years for Dave De K., who left Dean's body on Neeltje Jans
briefs.text: The court in Ghent sentenced him to 30 years in prison and 15 years of TBS for killing and kidnapping four-year-old Dean. His Dutch ex-girlfriend Romy W. was acquitted of kidnapping but convicted over images of child abuse.

sources.title: Dave De K. krijgt 30 jaar cel voor dood en ontvoering van 4-jarige Dean

briefs.title: Suspicious powder near the Covra site in Nieuwdorp proves harmless
briefs.text: Police, customs and the fire service closed the Italiëweg opposite Covra, the national radioactive-waste store, after a powder was found on Monday morning. Tests showed it was harmless and the road reopened in the early afternoon.

sources.title: Onderzoek na aantreffen verdachte stof bij Nieuwdorp

north-brabant.summary: The N65 upgrade is delayed for the sixth time, police say the suspect and the victim in the Beek en Donk killing were a couple, and a man fell into an open bin pit in Den Bosch.

briefs.title: Beek en Donk: suspect and victim were in a relationship
briefs.text: The body of a 50-year-old woman from Tilburg was found in a house in Beek en Donk early on Saturday. Police confirmed that the 56-year-old suspect and the woman were a couple; he is expected to be brought before a judge on Tuesday.

Verdachte en slachtoffer Beek en Donk hadden een relatie

briefs.title: Man falls into a three-metre bin pit in Den Bosch
briefs.text: An older man fell into the hole of an underground waste container that was being emptied on Monday morning and lay there for more than half an hour before being taken to hospital in Tilburg, Omroep Brabant reports.

sources.title: Oudere man valt in metersdiep gat van straatcontainer in Den Bosch

briefs.title: Wedding ring lost in 1942 found in Odiliapeel
briefs.text: A metal detectorist found the ring Jo Nabuurs lost while threshing behind the family farm in the winter of 1942–43, about 20 centimetres underground, and returned it to his son.

sources.title: Trouwring na 83 jaar teruggevonden in Brabants dorp: 'Nog in goede staat'

limburg.summary: Two people were hurt in a jewellery robbery in Maastricht, Brightlands was named the world's Intelligent Community of the Year, and five A76 viaducts keep their renewal money.

briefs.title: Two injured in robbery at a Maastricht jeweller
briefs.text: Jeweller Steiner on Stokstraat was robbed at about 10:40 on Monday and two people were injured. Police say the two men fled towards Onze Lieve Vrouweplein and the Maas.

sources.title: L1 Nieuws, 19 oktober 2026

briefs.title: Brightlands named Intelligent Community of the Year
briefs.text: The Intelligent Community Forum chose Limburg's four Brightlands campuses in Maastricht, Heerlen, Sittard-Geleen and Venlo, citing cooperation between government, business and research and the region's recovery since the mines closed. The Chemelot campus is now preparing to join a European pilot for faster permits and lower energy prices, L1 reports.

Limburg named the world's "most intelligent region"

briefs.title: Five A76 viaducts in South Limburg keep their funding
briefs.text: The renewal of five viaducts on the A76 is among the projects the cabinet still pays for in its new infrastructure plan, as is infrastructure for a large housing site in Weert.
